name: South Ridge
approach: Start at the Rainy Pass Picnic Area/Lake Ann trailhead on SR 20 (milepost ~157.5, elev. ~4,850 ft; 40-car lot with privy). Follow the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Trail (#740) about 1-1.5 miles to a signed junction and take the right fork toward Heather Pass (left continues to Lake Ann/Maple Pass loop). Climb through meadows to Heather Pass (~2.6 mi, ~6,100 ft), where the maintained trail ends. From the pass, pick up the unmarked climbers' path heading north, crossing two talus/boulder fields before dropping to Lewis Lake (~3.5-4 mi, ~5,700 ft; timbered campsites on the north side, water available) — this off-trail stretch is the main route-finding challenge of the approach, especially with cairns buried by early-season snow. From Lewis Lake, climb roughly 1,200 ft more of meadow and talus to Wing Lake (~5 mi, ~6,900 ft), the standard base camp, with sites in the trees on the right as you reach the lake and reliable water into late summer. From Wing Lake, go around the right (north) side of the lake and aim for the obvious talus/snow gully leading into the couloir just south of the summit; climb this gully, then angle climber's-right out of it to avoid cliff bands directly below the col, topping out at the south col on the crest of the south ridge — the true start of the climbing.

approach_variants.name: Rainy Pass and the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Trail to Heather Pass, then the unmarked path past Lewis Lake to Wing Lake
approach_variants.notes:
Start at the Rainy Pass Picnic Area and Lake Ann trailhead on SR-20 near milepost 157.5 at about 4,850 ft, a 40-car lot with a privy. This is the Rainy Pass Lake Ann, not the Lake Ann below Mount Shuksan on the Mount Baker Highway; the two are about 80 km apart and share a name.

Follow the Lake Ann and Maple Pass Trail #740 about 1-1.5 miles to a signed junction and take the right fork toward Heather Pass; the left continues on the Lake Ann and Maple Pass loop. Climb through meadows to Heather Pass at about 2.6 miles and 6,100 ft, where the maintained trail ends.

From the pass, pick up the unmarked climbers' path heading north, crossing two talus and boulder fields before dropping to Lewis Lake at about 3.5-4 miles and 5,700 ft, with timbered campsites on the north side and water. This off-trail stretch is the main route-finding challenge of the approach, especially with cairns buried by early-season snow. From Lewis Lake, climb roughly 1,200 ft more of meadow and talus to Wing Lake at about 5 miles and 6,900 ft, the standard base camp, with sites in the trees on the right as you reach the lake.
hazards: An unmarked off-trail stretch between Heather Pass and Lewis Lake, the approach's main route-finding challenge, worse with cairns buried by snow
Cliff bands directly below the south col if you climb the gully straight up rather than angling right
An exposed cairned ledge traverse below the summit block
A short class 4 step at the summit
Two lakes in Washington named Lake Ann; this route uses the Rainy Pass one
approach_variants.baseFinding:
Two lakes in sequence are the approach's spine, and they are water features, which is why this approach is survivable when the cairns are buried. Lewis Lake first, then about twelve hundred feet of climbing, then Wing Lake. If you have reached only one lake you are not at camp.

From Wing Lake, go around the right, north, side of the lake and aim for the obvious talus and snow gully leading into the couloir just south of the summit. Climb that gully, then angle climber's-right out of it to avoid cliff bands directly below the col, topping out at the south col on the crest of the south ridge. The south col is the true start of the climbing.

So the one instruction that keeps you out of trouble is the exit from the gully: angle right near the top. Going straight up puts you under cliff bands below the col.

Arrival at the col: a gap on a ridge crest with the summit pyramid to the north of you. Above it the route is cairned class 3 along the ridge to the summit pyramid, then a cairned class 2 ledge system traversing below the summit block, exposed near its end, and finally A short class 4 step of about 15 ft to the true summit.

So the count above the col is: cairned ridge, one ledge system, one 15 ft step. There is no other technical ground on this route. A boulder is slung at that step for an optional short rappel or hand line; a 30 m rope is more than enough, and many parties skip the rope and downclimb it facing in.

The discriminator against the peak's northeast ridge, which leaves the same camp: that route ascends snow toward the low point in the northeast ridge, following the Hogsback Moraine wide right and then traversing back left to the notch. Both routes cross moraine above the lake, so that alone tells you nothing; a notch on the northeast side instead of the south col means you are on the other route.

descent_text: This is the standard descent line for the peak — no separate down-route to learn. From the south col, downclimb along the cairned ridge (some class 3 moves) to the summit pyramid; the final section is a cairned class 2 ledge system traversing below the summit block that is exposed near its end, followed by a short (~15 ft) class 4 step to the true summit. On the way down, reverse this: downclimb the class 4 step (a boulder slung here permits a short optional rappel or hand-line — a single 30m rope is more than enough rope, and many parties skip the rope and downclimb it facing in), reverse the ledge traverse and the gully, and retrace the ridge back to the south col. From the col, descend the scree-and-snow slope (glissade-able early season) back down to Wing Lake, then hike out the approach trail. There is no mandatory multi-pitch rappel sequence on this route; the class 4 summit step is the only spot where climbers occasionally use a rope on the way down.

waypoints.name: Rainy Pass Trailhead (SR 20)
waypoints.note: Northwest Forest Pass required; parking is at the Rainy Pass picnic area, trailhead sign at the north end of the lot.
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR 20) to Rainy Pass near milepost 157.5, about 50 miles east of Marblemount or 35 miles west of Winthrop, and turn into the Rainy Pass Picnic Area on the south side of the highway; the Lake Ann/Maple Pass trailhead sign is at the north end of the lot. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. The highway closes for the winter over the pass.

waypoints.name: Heather Pass junction
waypoints.note: Leave the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Loop trail #740 here onto the unmaintained climbers' path toward Lewis and Wing Lakes.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Trail #740 about 1.3 miles through forest to the signed fork, stay right toward Heather Pass (the left fork goes to Lake Ann), and climb through meadows to Heather Pass, where you leave the maintained trail for the unmarked climbers' path toward Lewis and Wing Lakes.

waypoints.name: Talus field crossings
waypoints.note: Two loose talus fields to cross on the climbers' path before Lewis Lake; cairned but easy to lose in fog.
waypoints.directions: Follow the unmarked, cairned climbers' path west from Heather Pass across two loose talus and boulder fields. The cairns are easy to lose in fog or under early-season snow, and this is the main route-finding problem of the approach.

waypoints.name: Lewis Lake
waypoints.note: Lower, less-established camp option; only a couple of decent tent spots on the north shore.
waypoints.directions: Beyond the second talus field, drop down to Lewis Lake. The few tent sites are in the timber on the north shore.

waypoints.name: Wing Lake outlet
waypoints.note: Reliable water; the lake outlet is the last dependable source before the summit push.
waypoints.directions: From Lewis Lake, climb about 1,200 ft of meadow and talus west to Wing Lake.

waypoints.name: Wing Lake camp
waypoints.note: Standard base camp for Black Peak climbers; best established tent sites are here rather than Lewis Lake.
waypoints.directions: The established tent sites are in the trees on the right as you reach the lake, beside the outlet.

waypoints.name: South col
waypoints.note: Gained from Wing Lake by going around its north side, then up a moraine and permanent snowfield; a broad gully on the west side leads to the summit blocks.
waypoints.directions: Go around the right (north) side of Wing Lake, climb the moraine and permanent snowfield into the obvious talus and snow gully below the col, and angle climber's right out of it near the top to avoid the cliff bands directly below the col.

waypoints.name: Black Peak summit
waypoints.note: Class 3 with easy class 4 moves near the top; helmet recommended for rockfall off the summit block.
waypoints.directions: From the col, scramble north along the cairned south ridge toward the summit pyramid; a short class 4 step of about 15 ft guards the top.
